newsitem.title: UK: Ukraine power plant gets EBRD loan to modernise.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine power plant gets EBRD loan to modernise.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Tuesday it would lend $113 million to Ukraine to modernise its energy sector, leading the way to closure of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant.
The loan will be to state thermal power generator Donbasenergo Genco to replace a coal-fired boiler.

"This is a priority investment which will advance Ukraine's restructuring of its energy sector and the ultimate closure of the Chernobyl nuclear power station," EBRD energy team director Ananda Covindassamy said in a statement.
Ukraine has promised to shut the Chernobyl plant, site of the world's worst nuclear disaster in 1986, by 2000 in exchange for some $3.1 billion from the West.
The new boiler will use waste instead of expensive local coal and imported gas and oil.
"This means that Ukraine is able to use its locally produced coal more efficiently, ultimately reducing its energy usage and gas and oil imports," Covindassamy said.
The loan will cover 69 percent of the cost of a new 210 megawatt boiler using circulating fluidised bed boiler technology, which can burn low quality coal and residue of coal washing.
